definitions.gloss: abolition; eradication; doing away with entirely
definitions.explanation: Completely abolishing or wiping out something undesirable so that it ceases to exist. Often used of weapons, discrimination, and harmful customs.

examples.japanese: {核兵器|かくへいき}の{廃絶|はいぜつ}を{訴|うった}える。
examples.english: To call for the abolition of nuclear weapons.

examples.japanese: {差別|さべつ}の{廃絶|はいぜつ}を{目指|めざ}す{運動|うんどう}が{広|ひろ}がった。
examples.english: A movement aiming to eradicate discrimination spread.

examples.japanese: {被爆|ひばく}{国|こく}として、{日本|にほん}は{核兵器|かくへいき}の{廃絶|はいぜつ}を{世界|せかい}に{求|もと}め{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: As a country that suffered atomic bombing, Japan continues to call on the world to abolish nuclear weapons.

notes:
Compound of {廃|はい} (abolish, discard) + {絶|ぜつ} (sever, exterminate). A strong word implying total elimination, not mere reduction. Takes する as a transitive verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {核|かく}{廃絶|はいぜつ}: abolition of nuclear weapons
- {廃絶|はいぜつ}を{訴|うった}える: to call for abolition
- {廃絶|はいぜつ}を{目指|めざ}す: to aim at eradication

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {廃止|はいし}: abolition (of a system or rule) — repealing laws, institutions, or services
- {撲滅|ぼくめつ}: eradication; stamping out — campaigning to wipe out crime, disease, or evils
